items.title: Entry to relationships and the karmic tail M
items.lead: The first inner reaction that starts both closeness and the old script.
items.formula: The sum of the karmic task D and the centre E.
meaning: Point M stands between the karmic task D and the centre of the chart E, and it is their sum. It shows the first reaction at the moment a situation becomes genuinely personal. One person moves straight towards closeness, another checks whether it is safe, a third hides behind control or a joke. The end of the story is not in this point, but its emotional start is easy to see.

Two different routes run out of M. In relationships it is M→R1→R: the way into closeness, the partner point and the way of building a union. In the karmic tail it is M→N→D: the first impulse, its lesson and the way out to the karmic task. So the same arcanum does not get one universal reading — the context of the line changes the question.

M has one feature you notice at once on your own chart: the numbers here are always multiples of three. There are only seven possible values — 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 21. That is how the formula works, and no other number can stand in this place for any date of birth. If a reading names, say, a ten here, it is talking about the neighbouring point of the relationship line, not about the entry.

A strong side of M is catching your first impulse before it has turned into a familiar script. For example, not declaring a partner’s silence to be rejection, and not answering a new situation with an old defence. A weak side is treating the automatic reaction as the only one possible and being surprised by the same ending every time. A useful way to read the point is to compare your last two episodes of closeness with two conflicts that keep repeating: where the reaction was the same, while the meaning and what followed turned out different.
items.reading: First decide the context: M–R1–R is read as relationships, M–N–D as the tail. The same M does not turn these two triples into one program.

items.title: Under the heart — the partner point R1
items.lead: The middle of the relationship line: what surfaces in a couple once the first attraction has passed.
items.formula: The sum of the entry to the relationship line M and the point where money and relationships cross, R.
meaning: The partner point is almost always called the one “under the heart”: on the scheme it sits right below the centre of the chart, which is usually drawn as a heart. In the method it has a name and a formula — R1, the middle of the relationship line M → R1 → R. It is counted in two steps: first the crossing of money and relationships R, as the sum of the relationship entry M and the money line entry L, then the point itself as the sum of M and R.

The entry of the line, M, answers for the first reaction to getting close, while R1 answers for what a couple starts to revolve around once the discovering is over and life together has begun. For one person that is about honesty and keeping score, for another about freedom, for a third about care that quietly turns into control. The arcanum here describes not the partner, but what a person brings into the couple on the second step.

Telling this point apart from the entry is easiest by the number. Point M only takes numbers that divide by three: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21. The partner point takes any number from 3 to 22. So a “ten under the heart” or an “eleventh arcanum under the heart” is always R1, and there is no reason to mix it up with the entry of the line.

This point explains why things repeat: why with different people the conversation runs into the same wall. The script is set not by the partner’s character but by the question a person carries in with them. Until that question is said out loud, it gets settled at the couple’s expense — and comes back in the next couple. That is why R1 is read as part of the whole line and not on its own: the entry M shows how it all starts, the crossing R shows what it runs into, and the partner point between them answers what the couple is holding together for.
items.reading: Compare R1 with the entry M: if they mean much the same, the couple repeats the first impulse and quickly runs into its price; if they differ, the second stage asks for something other than what the attraction began with.

items.lead: The third level: the sum of the personal and social purposes.

meaning: This level appears where personal work and being useful to other people stop pulling in opposite directions. It is not abstract enlightenment but a fairly down-to-earth state: a person does what matters to them, other people need it, and neither side has to be betrayed for the sake of the other.

In the reading it turns up twice: in the purpose section and as the point of exit from repeating programs. That makes sense — a story stops going round in circles exactly where a person acts in agreement with themselves, not out of inertia and not out of spite.
items.reading: Look for an occupation that leaves behind neither emptiness nor guilt. The arcanum of spiritual purpose describes the agreement between the personal and the social, not abstract calm.

meaning: Planetary purpose is put together from the social and spiritual levels. Family branches reach it through the social level, but they are not added in directly at this step. The name sounds grand, and the thing itself looks ordinary — a teacher who has seen thirty classes out of the door, or a third-generation engineer.

The point should not be read as a duty to save the world. The practical question is gentler: what do you do that will outlive you by a couple of generations? If there is no answer at all, that is not a verdict but a hint about where to look once the personal levels are closed.

items.title: Personal purpose
items.lead: What you need to do for yourself, no matter how others rate it.
items.formula: The sum of the sky line B–D and earth line A–C totals.
meaning: Personal purpose in the destiny matrix is the first point of the purpose zone and the closest one to the person: the task they come here to carry out not for the family, not for society and not for the world, but for themselves. It is about who they have to become, which qualities to grow and what to give up inside. Nobody hands out rewards from the outside for this — and that is the main difficulty of the position.

The purpose zone in the chart is built in levels, from the particular to the general, and the personal level stands right at the start of it — it is the foundation. Its sense is that a person first puts their own life and character in order, and only after that can their energy really work for others. The point is responsible for inner support: for whether a person lives their own life or somebody else’s.

This position shows which way a person has to grow personally: which lessons they came to go through themselves, what to stop tolerating, where to stop pleasing others. It affects the sense of self, the ability to choose in your own favour without guilt, and whether a person feels they are in the right place.

When the point works, a person is busy with their own development without an eye on approval, calmly spends time and strength on what matters to them and does not wait for it to be appreciated. When it is weak, life is built around other people’s expectations: plenty of help given, plenty of praise received, and emptiness inside with no clue where your own part is. While the personal level stays unclosed, the next levels of purpose do not switch on at full strength.

items.lead: What people know you for and how you are useful to many.

meaning: Social purpose in the destiny matrix is the point of the second, social level of purpose. It shows through which work a person becomes needed not only by themselves and those close to them, but by a wide circle of strangers, and what those people know and value them for. If the personal level of purpose is about what you master for yourself, the social one covers the contribution that goes beyond the home and turns into a recognisable role.

By meaning the point stands in the middle of the purpose scale — between what you do for yourself and the highest, planetary task. So it is about a bridge: the place where a personal gift meets the demand of society and adds up to a calling rather than just a way to earn. What counts here is not the job title in a work record, but the work people come back to you for.

The point at full strength is easy to recognise: a person has a name in their niche, people come to them for something specific, their contribution is visible and earns a reputation. Weak is when the gift stays with its owner: the talent is there, but the role others lean on is not; the person feels they are in the wrong place and underused.

Social purpose affects the choice of a profession as a calling, the scale and the circle of people your usefulness reaches, and the feeling of being needed. It is not a promise of fame and not a forecast of particular events, but a direction in which your work stops being private and starts working for many.
